DAY 01:
LONDON – GRETNA GREEN (WHISKY TASTING) – GLASGOW

JOURNEY TO SCOTLAND
After meeting your tour manager at your designated pick-up point, settle comfortably into your coach as we begin our journey north. As we cross into Scotland, our first stop is the romantic and historic village of Gretna Green.

VISIT TO GRETNA GREEN
Our first stop is the romantic and historic village of Gretna Green.

FAMOUS BLACKSMITHS SHOP
At Gretna Green’s Famous Blacksmiths Shop, discover over 260 years of tradition, where generations of eloping couples pledged their vows over the blacksmith’s anvil. Today, the site is a charming visitor attraction featuring heritage exhibits, boutique shopping, and inviting restaurants – although you may want to resist the temptation to tie the knot yourself!

MALT WHISKY TASTING EXPERIENCE
Immerse yourself in Scotland’s whisky heritage with a guided tasting. Learn how Scotch whisky is crafted, uncover the characteristics of its distinct regions, and enjoy sampling two malt whiskies and a Scottish liqueur.

PANORAMIC TOUR OF GLASGOW
We then continue to the vibrant city of Glasgow for a panoramic tour showcasing some of its most iconic landmarks, including:

  • Glasgow Cathedral – the city’s oldest building and a masterpiece of Scottish Gothic architecture
  • George Square – Glasgow’s historic civic heart and cultural hub
  • University of Glasgow – one of the UK’s oldest and most esteemed universities
  • Additional key sights that embody Glasgow’s dynamic character

In the evening, savour a delicious Indian dinner before checking in to the hotel for a comfortable overnight stay.

MEALS: D

DAY 02:
GLASGOW – FALKIRK WHEEL – THE KELPIES – EDINBURGH – GLASGOW

DEPART FOR EDINBURGH
After breakfast, we begin our journey toward Scotland’s historic capital, Edinburgh, with exciting stops along the way.

THE FALKIRK WHEEL
Our first experience of the day is the Falkirk Wheel – the world’s only rotating boat lift and a remarkable feat of modern engineering. This unique structure links the Forth & Clyde Canal with the Union Canal through a graceful half‑turn rotation that takes just five minutes, offering a fascinating blend of innovation and design.

THE KELPIES AT HELIX PARK
Next, we visit Helix Park, home to The Kelpies – the world’s largest equine sculptures. Standing 100 feet tall and weighing over 300 tonnes each, these shimmering steel giants pay tribute to Scotland’s powerful working horses that once ploughed fields and pulled barges along the nation’s waterways.

ARRIVAL IN EDINBURGH & ORIENTATION TOUR
We then make our way to the magnificent capital city of Edinburgh. Upon arrival, we head to our selected restaurant for lunch before beginning an orientation tour featuring key highlights such as:

  • Princes Street – Edinburgh’s famous shopping and cultural boulevard
  • Palace of Holyroodhouse – the King’s official residence in Scotland
  • Additional notable landmarks showcasing the city’s rich heritage

After the tour, stroll along the historic Royal Mile to admire St Giles’ Cathedral, celebrated for its striking crown‑shaped spire and centuries of history.

EDINBURGH CASTLE
Next, we visit the iconic Edinburgh Castle, dramatically perched atop an ancient volcanic rock. Dominating the city skyline for centuries, the castle invites you to explore its grand state apartments and view the ancient Scottish Crown Jewels.

DINNER & RETURN TO GLASGOW
In the evening, enjoy a delicious dinner at one of our selected restaurants before returning to Glasgow for your overnight stay.

MEALS: B, L, D

DAY 03:
GLASGOW – NEVIS RANGE – COMMANDO MEMORIAL – GLENFINNAN VIADUCT – NEPTUNE’S STAIRCASE – GLASGOW

JOURNEY TO THE HIGHLANDS
After breakfast, channel your inner Highlander as we embark on a scenic journey north to the banks of Loch Lomond and beyond.

NEVIS RANGE & CABLE CAR RIDE
We continue along the picturesque route towards Fort William to visit the Nevis Range. Upon arrival, enjoy a cable car ride to the upper station, rising high above sea level and offering breathtaking views of Ben Nevis, the highest mountain in the British Isles. This ancient giant was once a massive active volcano, which erupted and collapsed millions of years ago – truly the pinnacle of Scotland!

COMMANDO MEMORIAL
Next, we make a photo stop at the Commando Memorial, a Category A listed structure standing 17 ft (5.2 m) high. This striking bronze sculpture depicts three World War II commandos in full uniform, including cap comforters, ammunition pouches, and weapons. The monument honours the officers and men of the commandos who gave their lives between 1939–1945.

GLENFINNAN VIADUCT & MEMORIAL
Later, we head to the Glenfinnan Visitor Centre for a photo stop at the famous Glenfinnan Viaduct and Glenfinnan Monument. The viaduct, built between 1897–1901, is part of the West Highland Line in Inverness‑shire and overlooks Loch Shiel. It has appeared in several films, most famously in four of the Harry Potter movies. The Glenfinnan Monument, erected in 1815, commemorates the Jacobite clansmen who fought for Prince Charles Edward Stuart. Standing 18 metres high, it features a lone kilted highlander at the top – a poignant tribute to the fallen clansmen.

NEPTUNE’S STAIRCASE
Our final stop of the day is Neptune’s Staircase, a remarkable staircase lock on the Caledonian Canal. Originally hand‑powered, it now operates hydraulically, comprising eight locks that raise and lower boats along this historic waterway.

DINNER & RETURN TO GLASGOW
End the day with a delicious dinner at one of our selected restaurants before returning to your hotel in Glasgow for an overnight stay.

MEALS: B, D

DAY 04:
GLASGOW – LAKE DISTRICT – LONDON

DEPARTURE FROM GLASGOW
After breakfast, check out from the hotel and settle in for a scenic drive south toward the Lake District, England’s largest and most picturesque national park.

EXPLORING THE LAKE DISTRICT
The Lake District is renowned for its breathtaking scenery, abundant wildlife, and rich cultural heritage. Our visit includes Lake Windermere, the largest lake in England, situated in the heart of this stunning region.

LAKE WINDERMERE CRUISE
Step aboard for a cruise on Lake Windermere, enjoying magnificent views of mountains, secluded bays, and wooded islands. This relaxing journey offers a unique perspective of the area’s natural beauty.

HERITAGE STEAM TRAIN EXPERIENCE
Next, experience a heritage steam train ride between Haverthwaite and Lakeside, evoking the charm of a bygone era. Whether a nostalgic memory for some or a new adventure for others, this journey provides a delightful glimpse into England’s railway history.

RETURN TO LONDON
In the late afternoon, we begin our drive back to our respective drop‑off points, bidding farewell to new friends and cherishing memories of an unforgettable tour.

MEALS: B

IMPORTANT PICK‑UP INFORMATION
It is important that you are at the pick-up point at least 15 minutes before the coach departure time as the coach or pick up vehicle will not wait for passengers coming late. If you miss the pickup at the appointed time, it will be your responsibility to get to the next destination on your itinerary at your own expense. No refund will be allowed in any circumstances if you do not continue with the tour. Please be on time, as we cannot be held responsible or liable for any loss or expenses suffered if you miss the coach.

Note: For logistic reasons Manta Holidays reserves the right to change the timings of any pick up one day prior to departure and the right to change coaches during the trip.

TRAVEL INSURANCE
Because of the importance of having adequate insurance cover, we suggest all our clients to be covered by an insurance policy before travelling on your booked holiday. If you elect not to take out insurance, you agree to indemnify Gowri Tours for any costs that arise which would otherwise have been met if you had your own travel insurance.

WHEELCHAIRS
We do not provide a specialist tour for less abled, however every attempt will be made to accommodate you to our best ability. It is possible to bring along a folding type of wheelchair which may be kept in the baggage hold of the coach. The driver will load and unload the wheelchair from the coach for the passenger; however, they will need to be physically fit enough to be able to embark and disembark the coach on their own. It is also essential that a capable person is accompanying such a passenger on the tour to push their wheelchair. We will also request hotels for suitably equipped rooms; however, this is only on a request basis and cannot be guaranteed. All wheelchairs need to be collapsible and electric wheelchairs cannot be stored on any of our coaches.

ESSENTIALS TO CARRY WITH YOU
Long journeys are unavoidable, and we recommend you wear comfortable clothing and carry essentials such as a jacket or jumper, dry snacks, water, tissues, chargers, power bank etc., in your handbag as access to the luggage hold may not be possible until a comfort stop or arrival at your destination. Hot foods are not allowed to be carried or consumed inside the coach.

COACHES
All coaches are fitted with armrests, TV, DVD & CD player, and WC facilities. WC facilities on coaches have limited capacities and therefore we advise passengers to use them only on an “emergency” basis as once it is full it will be locked. We will try to make sufficient comfort stops. On rare occasions, your coach may not have a WC, TV, DVD player facility on board. All coaches are either air-conditioned or air-cooled. We have a strict “no smoking” policy on all our coaches. Consumption of alcohol is prohibited on all our coaches. During transfers, we may use an alternative vehicle (smaller coaches/car) which may not have the above facilities. For your own safety seat belts must always be worn when you are inside the vehicle.

BAGGAGE ON COACH
Each passenger occupying a seat is allowed to carry one piece of luggage whose maximum weight should not be more than 20kg and not exceeding dimensions of 90 x 75 x 43cm / 35 x 29 x 16 inches and one piece of hand luggage whose weight should not be more than 8kg and not exceeding dimensions of 20 x 20 x 48 cm / 8 x 8 x 19 inches which can fit under the seat or in the overhead compartment. The main luggage will be placed inside the coach locker and the passenger will only get access to the same when we reach your destination. The driver will load and unload one piece of luggage per person from the coach. It is advisable to put your name and address on each piece of luggage as many passengers have similar bags and this avoids confusion. If for any reasons your baggage or personal valuable is lost or stolen, you must report it to the tour manager, or in the absence of a tour manager to the local police. We cannot accept any responsibility for your personal belongings. All baggage is placed at the owner’s risk, and we accept no liability for loss or damage to bags caused anyhow.

CHILDREN & YOUNG INFANTS
Children and young infants are welcome to travel on our tours. Children under the age of 23 months will be charged an infant fare on all tours. Car/booster seats are not provided on coaches by us, and it is strongly recommended carrying your own which can fit within the coach seats. Coaches will not provide any cold or hot water to heat up or cool milk bottles. It is passengers’ responsibility to make sure of necessary arrangements for any children in their group. Pushchairs will be kept in the luggage compartment of the coach. Children’s or infants will not be seated at the front of the coach.

TOUR MANAGER
Professional tour manager/driver or local guides will accompany throughout your itinerary on all our escorted tours. On rare occasions, your tour manager may not meet you at your dedicated pick-up point but at a later stage; the driver will be there to take care of your needs. On rare occasions, a tour manager will not be available to accompany you; this would be due to unavoidable operational issues, or we will be utilising local guides for their wealth of experience. On rare occasion on some of our tours, there will be no accompanying tour manager and our expert driver or local tour guide will conduct the tour.

WEATHER, CLOTHING & ACCESSORIES
It is recommended to always carry an umbrella and a jacket. We recommend that you visit www.weather.com to ensure you have an idea of the weather at the time of the year you want to travel and can be well prepared by ensuring that you are carrying appropriate clothing, footwear, and accessories. Passengers should also be aware that some sightseeing would be done after dusk. During summer months, it is advisable to wear light garments during the day but keep a light jacket or sweater in your hand luggage for the evening, as it can be quite chilly. Also, few other items which are highly recommended are a family sized umbrella, rain wear, pair of sunglasses, pair of trainers or comfortable walking shoes especially for certain excursions that involve a considerable amount of walking. Smart clothes will be required if you wish to go to a casino or nightclub. We also recommend passengers to carry a small travel iron, hairdryer, kettle etc. as not all hotels may provide the same in the rooms. You may also be required to be “covered” up when visiting certain places; if you are unsure what to take then please do discuss with us and we will be happy to assist.

HOTELS
The hotels on our tours are selected carefully to ensure that a minimum 3* category is provided and can be located either close to the city you are visiting or on the outskirts. Facilities vary from hotel to hotel and include en-suite bath or shower and generally a TV and telephone. Some of the rooms may have mini bars and 24-hour room service. You will be charged if you use any payable facilities at the hotel to your room and payable on departure. Most hotels may require a credit card to cover your extras or cash deposits. Not all hotels will have air-conditioning or lift as standard. If you have difficulty with stairs, please advise us so we can try to request a room on a lower floor. Rooms are also allocated by the hotel so some guests may get larger or different type of rooms to other guests. We do not have control over this.

Note: We reserve the right to substitute hotels whilst passengers are on tour to a similar standard due to unforeseen circumstances. Please note that hotel’s normal check-in times are from late afternoon, e.g. 3pm and checkout around 11am, but it does vary from hotel to hotel.

ROOM CONFIGURATION
Most hotels can only accommodate a maximum of three persons in each room. If you are a family of four, i.e., two adults and two children, and prefer all to be in one room, then your first child will be given an extra bed, but the second child will be required to share the double bed as no extra bed can be provided. The extra bed provided will be either a sofa bed or rollaway bed. These extra beds may not be full sized as double beds and are usually suitable for one individual only. The cost of the package is based on a minimum of two adults sharing one room. If your group consists of one adult and one child, the child must pay a full adult fare to make up the cost for the room required. Baby cots are not guaranteed. When you opt for two rooms, each room must have an adult accompanying a child as per regulations of the hotel. A child will always have to be accompanied by an adult in a room. We will try our best to get these 2 rooms next to each other but can’t guarantee the same. Where a quad room is not available for your group, a reduction will be given as stated in the itinerary. Note that quad rooms have limited space and additional beds may not be suitable for tall adults. Any damages within the room or hotel you are staying in will be payable at the time of departure by the passenger.

MEALS
Breakfast is normally continental buffet, which will be served in the hotel that you will be staying. All other pre-booked meals will be at an outside restaurant and is not changeable. Passengers may have an option to choose from vegetarian or non-vegetarian (wherever possible Jain/Halal) meals. The meals will only include the food; all extras i.e., alcohol, beverages or any extra items requested by you will need to be settled by you directly with the restaurant. Any meals not taken will not be reimbursed under any circumstances. On some days, you may be provided with packed dinner to suit the itinerary of a particular tour. We endeavour to book Indian meals for dinner wherever possible, however due to local constraints if we are unable to do so, we will offer local vegetarian options. If you have any specific dietary needs or allergies, you must inform us at the time of booking, so we can inform the caterer. However, special arrangements for food cannot be guaranteed for allergies or requests such as Halal or Jain meals. Passengers with severe food allergies are advised to make appropriate arrangements prior to commencing their tour. We reserve the right to change meal arrangement in circumstances that are beyond our control.

If for any reason we are unable to provide the meal, we will refund the passenger with 10 GBP per person per dinner.

SEATING, DIETARY OR ROOM ALLOCATION AND OTHER REQUESTS
We work with intermediary agents (hotels, transport companies, other suppliers etc.) to arrange your holiday. If passengers have special requirements such as a rooming request, or a special meal request etc., then they should advise us at the time of booking. Any special requests cannot be guaranteed by us. Seating requests are not taken under any circumstance. Seating is allocated by booking reference number however, there are some exceptions to this, i.e., group sizes, coach size, promotional seating, H&S laws, pickups, company discretion etc. We do not promise or guarantee any specific seat on the coach, and we have the sole right to assign your seats. Any indication is for reference only and is subject to change regardless of whether given in writing or any other means. Seat numbers will be informed to all passengers on the day of departure. Groups with children will not be seated in the front of the coach even if they have booked very early. Some seats in the coach may not recline. Passengers who do not want to book under the same booking reference number but wish to travel together must inform us at the time of booking so they can be seated next to each other. Any medical, and/or personal grounds are not considered when allocating seats, unless explicitly stated by law or governing bodies.

LOST PROPERTY & THEFT
It is passenger’s responsibility to ensure that your property and valuables are always safe. If an item has been left in the coach, you will need to call the respective supplier and arrange with them directly for the return of your item. We will not carry anyone’s property across international borders whether it is authorised in writing or by any other means. In case of theft, you will need to advise your tour manager immediately and report the theft to the nearest police personnel who will provide you with a police report or crime reference number. You are advised not to carry unnecessary valuables and to be always vigilant, as tourist spots are well known targets for pickpockets. We recommend all passengers to have valid travel insurance, including EU citizens.

LONG DISTANCE JOURNEYS
Some journeys can be long, and they are unavoidable when travelling from one city to another. Hence, we recommend on such long journey days to wear comfortable clothes. As most part of these days will be spent inside the coach, we advise passengers to carry all necessities that they may need for the day such as water, dry snacks, tissues, medication, chargers, power banks etc. with them in their hand luggage.

EXCURSIONS

These times may be modified without notice by the management due to exceptional events, unfavourable weather conditions, large numbers of visitors, or a Force Majeure event. Access to the excursions/monuments depends on the type of ticket purchased, and all exits are final; no re-entries are permitted. Tickets issued are for immediate entry. In the case of loss or theft, the tickets cannot be reimbursed. Certain excursions may restrict access due to saturation.

ITINERARY & TIME KEEPING
The tour manager reserves the right to modify the itinerary during the tour. These changes may occur due to unexpected delays, major local events that can often arise or a Force Majeure event. Time keeping is the most important aspect of a group tour and all passengers must adhere to the timings given by their tour manager. All our holiday packages are subject to governance by DVSA for driving hours hence it is the passenger’s responsibility to ensure all departure times are respected. We will not take responsibility for passengers left behind due to not adhering to itineraries and times stated by the tour manager for whatsoever reason, and any subsequent impact this may cause financially or non-financially. It is a passenger’s responsibility to ensure that they are clear in understanding of the departure time from any given point. If in any doubt, please make sure that you recheck the departure timings again with your tour manager and follow the same.

We request you to go through the general information and Terms & Conditions before booking and travelling.

LONDON - SOUTHAMPTON/PORTSMOUTH - SHANKLIN BEACH - THE NEEDLES - LONDON

EMBARK ON A SCENIC ISLAND ADVENTURE
After a warm welcome from your tour manager at your designated pick-up point, settle into your comfortable coach as we begin our scenic journey towards Southampton or Portsmouth. From here, we take a short and pleasant ferry crossing over the Solent to England’s largest island – the Isle of Wight.

SHANKLIN BEACH – GOLDEN SANDS & SEASIDE CHARM
Our first stop is the picturesque Shanklin Beach, one of the island’s most loved coastal gems. This beautiful stretch of golden sand is backed by a classic English promenade, offering plenty of charm and stunning sea views. Enjoy free time here to relax, stroll along the beachfront, or capture postcard-perfect photos.

THE NEEDLES & ALUM BAY – ICONIC VIEWS OF THE ISLE OF WIGHT
We then continue to the island’s most famous landmark, The Needles, located at Alum Bay. Renowned for its striking multi-coloured sand cliffs, this area offers breathtaking views across the Solent. You may choose to take the optional chairlift ride (ticket not included) for a delightful descent from the clifftops to the beach, treating you to panoramic sights of the Needles Rocks, lighthouse, and the turquoise waters below.

RETURN TO LONDON
After immersing yourself in the natural beauty and unique landscapes of Alum Bay, we begin our journey back to the mainland by ferry, returning to Southampton or Portsmouth. We then proceed towards your respective drop-off points, bidding farewell to the new friends you’ve made on this unforgettable day trip.

DAY 1: LONDON – OSBORNE HOUSE – RYDE BEACH – SANDOWN

After a warm welcome from your tour manager at your designated pick-up point, relax in the comfort of your coach as we begin our scenic journey towards either Southampton or Portsmouth. Just a short sea crossing over the Solent, we arrive at England’s largest island – the Isle of Wight. Known for its charming countryside and stunning coastline, the island offers a perfect blend of history, nature, and traditional seaside charm.

OSBORNE HOUSE
Get an unforgettable glimpse into the private family life of Queen Victoria and Prince Albert at Osborne on the Isle of Wight. From sumptuous interiors and art collections inside, to a peaceful beach and marvellous gardens outside, a day out at Osborne has something for everyone. Explore Osborne’s vast grounds, follow the interactive tree trail and find the unusual Swiss Cottage, where the royal children played, gardened, cooked and collected unusual objects in their own private museum.

RYDE BEACH
Our next stop will be Ryde Beach, a large, sandy beach on the northeast coast of the Isle of Wight, known for its long, flat expanse and proximity to Ryde town and pier. It is popular for a wide range of activities, from sunbathing and sandcastle building to water sports, and offers numerous facilities like eateries and amusements.

CHECK-IN AT OUR HOTEL – SANDOWN BEACH
In the late evening, we check into our hotel located right on the beautiful Sandown Beach – one of the Isle of Wight’s most celebrated sandy stretches. This bustling, family-friendly seaside resort features a traditional pier with amusements, crazy golf, and more. The Sandown Esplanade is lined with cafes, beach shops, and attractions, while the nearby high street offers everything from artisan stores to pubs and restaurants.

FREE TIME TO EXPLORE SANDOWN
After check-in, the rest of the day is yours to enjoy at leisure. Explore Sandown Beach, stroll the pier, indulge in local treats, or shop for souvenirs. Soak in the lively yet relaxed atmosphere of this traditional English seaside town before making your way back to the hotel at your own pace.

DAY 2: PEARL FACTORY – THE NEEDLES – LONDON

After a hearty breakfast at the hotel, we check out and begin the next leg of our island adventure.

ISLE OF WIGHT PEARL – JEWELLERY, VIEWS & REFRESHMENTS
Our first visit is to the elegant Isle of Wight Pearl, located along the breathtaking Military Road on the island’s southwest coast. Browse a stunning collection of handcrafted pearl jewellery, from timeless classics to contemporary designs. Learn about the origins of pearls, pearl grading, and jewellery-making in the informative displays. Relax at the Pearl Café, offering sweeping views of the English Channel – perfect for a quick tea or coffee with a view. This is a unique island experience blending craftsmanship, coastal beauty, and peaceful indulgence.

THE NEEDLES – A COASTAL ICON
Next, we make our way to one of the most iconic natural landmarks in the UK – The Needles. Marvel at the multi-coloured sand cliffs of Alum Bay. See the famous Needles Rocks and lighthouse, perched majestically in the turquoise waters of the Solent.

Optional: Take the scenic chairlift (ticket not included) from the clifftop down to the beach – an unforgettable ride with panoramic views. Don’t forget your camera – this is one of the most photographed spots in the world for a reason!

After soaking in the views and seaside atmosphere at The Needles, we begin our journey back to take our ferry to Southampton or Portsmouth. Travel onward to your original drop-off point, reminiscing about the memories and friendships made.

As our Isle of Wight journey ends, we bid a fond farewell to the island and to the new friends made along the way. Thank you for joining us on this unforgettable escape.

DAY 1:

London - Calais - Brussels

After a warm welcome from your tour manager at your designated pick-up point, settle into your comfortable coach as we begin our journey across the English Channel. Upon arrival in Calais or Dunkerque, we travel onwards into Belgium.

Arrival in Brussels - Walking Tour of the Old Town

Our first stop is the charming city of Brussels, where we begin with a guided walking tour of the historic old town. At the heart of the city lies the La Grand Place, one of the most beautiful and photographed squares in Europe. Surrounded by stunning guildhalls, the Town Hall, and the King's House (also known as the Bread House), this UNESCO World Heritage Site is a true architectural masterpiece. The King's House also houses the Museum of the City of Brussels, offering insights into the city's rich heritage.

Nearby, you'll encounter the bronze statue of Everard t'Serclaes, a local hero who died defending Brussels in the 15th century.
Legend has it that touching his arm brings good luck.

Manneken Pis - A Beloved Symbol

A short walk leads us to Manneken Pis, a quirky and iconic statue that represents the spirit of Brussels. Created in 1388, this small 50m bronze figure of a boy urinating into a fountain has long been one of the city's favourite symbols. It originally served as a public water source and is located just off the Grand Place, between Rue de l'Étuve and Rue du Chêne.

Photo Stop at The Atomium

Next, we take a photo stop at the Atomium, the most iconic structure in Brussels. Standing 102 meters tall, this futuristic stainless-steel model of an atom was built for the 1958 Brussels World's Fair and remains a powerful symbol of innovation. Today, the Atomium is to Brussels what the Eiffel Tower is to Paris.

Journey to Hotel

In the evening, we depart Brussels and head towards our hotel. Upon arrival, we enjoy a delicious Indian dinner at a local restaurant before checking into our hotel for our two-night stay. Get ready to explore more of the Amsterdam in the days ahead.

DAY 2:

A Day of Dutch Delights: Tulips, Traditions & Timeless

Amsterdam

Fall in love with the Netherlands in a single unforgettable day! From world-famous flower fields to iconic canals, this carefully curated experience blends natural beauty, cultural heritage, and the irresistible charm.

Keukenhof Tulip Gardens - A Floral Wonderland

Your adventure begins at the breathtaking Keukenhof, one of the world's largest and most spectacular flower gardens. Wander through 32 hectares of vibrant colour, where 7 million spring-flowering bulbs bloom in imaginative themed displays. Sculptures, art installations, and ever-changing annual themes make every visit truly unique.

After 10 May, when Keukenhof closes for the season, this visit will be replaced with an excursion to

Madurodam - The famous miniature city in The Hague.

At Madurodam, you'll explore 1:25 scale models of iconic Dutch landmarks-including castles, historic buildings, industrial projects, and more. Guests enjoy a delightful journey through Dutch history and architecture, with plenty of interactive, hands-on exhibits that bring the country's story to life.

Cheese & Clog Farm - A Taste of Dutch Tradition

In the early afternoon, we head to a traditional Cheese and Clog Farm. Watch a craftsman transform a simple block of wood into a classic Dutch clog, then step into the old cheese room to learn the art of making Gouda cheese and the history behind the farm. A tasting follows, where you'll sample a range of delicious farm-made Gouda varieties. Later enjoy some free tome for shopping.

Amsterdam Canal Cruise - The Heart of the Dutch Capital Arrive in the enchanting city of Amsterdam, where a glass-topped canal cruise offers the perfect introduction. Glide along 100 km of scenic waterways, passing grand merchant houses, gothic churches, charming bridges, and medieval landmarks. Live commentary brings the city's history and hidden gems to life as you soak in breathtaking waterfront views.

Free Time at Damrak - The City's Vibrant Core

After your cruise, enjoy free time along Damrak, Amsterdam's bustling central boulevard filled with shops, cafés, and photo-worthy

sights-equally lively by day and night.

Your day concludes with a delicious dinner at a local Indian restaurant before settling in for your final night in the Netherlands.

DAY 3:

Bruges - London

After breakfast, we check out of the hotel and begin our journey to Bruges, a city that leaves a lasting impression on every visitor. Often called the "Venice of the North," Bruges is one of Europe's best-preserved medieval cities and a proud UNESCO World Heritage City.

Guided Walking Tour of Historic Bruges

We will explore Bruges' enchanting old town with a local

guide as you stroll through its cobbled lanes and scenic canals. Highlights
include Begijnhof - a serene courtyard founded in the 13th century, St.
Saviour's Cathedral - the city's oldest parish church, Market Square (Markt) -
the vibrant heart of Bruges, surrounded by medieval architecture & many
more timeless landmarks that showcase the city's Gothic charm. Take in the
beauty of this captivating city, renowned for its tranquil waterways, historic
buildings, and postcard-perfect scenery.

Channel Crossing to Dover

In the late afternoon, we return to our coach and travel to
Calais or Dunkerque for our channel crossing to Dover. Upon arrival in England,
you will proceed to your respective drop-off points, bidding farewell to the

DAY 1:
LONDON – CALAIS/DUNKERQUE – OVERNIGHT JOURNEY

YOUR EUROPEAN ADVENTURE BEGINS

EVENING DEPARTURE FROM LONDON
This evening, after a warm welcome from your tour manager at your designated pick-up point, settle into your comfortable, air‑conditioned coach as we begin our exciting journey across Europe.

CHANNEL CROSSING TO MAINLAND EUROPE
We travel south to the coast for our Channel crossing via Calais or Dunkerque, continuing our route toward the heart of Europe. Sit back, relax, and enjoy the smooth transition from the UK into continental Europe.

OVERNIGHT JOURNEY TO SWITZERLAND
As we make our way through scenic landscapes, take time to unwind, get to know your fellow travellers, or simply enjoy the peaceful night drive. By morning, you’ll be approaching beautiful Switzerland, where your unforgettable adventure truly begins!

DAY 2:
RHINE FALLS – ZURICH

NATURE’S POWER & SWITZERLAND’S URBAN CHARM

MORNING BREAK & SCENIC DRIVE THROUGH THE BLACK FOREST
In the morning, we stop at services where you can freshen up and enjoy breakfast at your own leisure. We then continue our journey through the enchanting Black Forest region of Germany, whose lush landscapes provide the perfect backdrop for this scenic morning drive. Soon after, we cross into Switzerland for our first highlight of the day.

RHINE FALLS – EUROPE’S LARGEST WATERFALL
Our first stop is Schaffhausen, home to the breathtaking Rhine Falls – Europe’s biggest waterfall. Marvel at the immense power of water as huge masses cascade over a 150‑metre‑wide stretch of rock. For the adventurous, don’t miss the thrilling boat ride and climb to the middle rock, offering an unforgettable vantage point of this natural wonder. Enjoy some free time to explore the area, take photos, or simply admire the stunning views.

ARRIVAL IN ZURICH – THE CITY BY THE WATER
We then travel to Zurich, a vibrant city where modern urban living blends harmoniously with natural beauty. Enjoy free time to explore key sights such as:

  • Fraumünster Church – recognisable by its elegant green steeple
  • Grossmünster Church – a landmark Protestant church steeped in history
  • A leisurely stroll along the Limmat River
  • Lake Zurich – a beautiful, curved lake perfect for relaxing walks and scenic views

Zurich offers a perfect mix of culture, architecture, and tranquil waterside charm.

DINNER & HOTEL CHECK‑IN
After your free time in Zurich, we head to a local restaurant for a delicious dinner before checking into our hotel for a comfortable overnight stay.

MEALS: D

DAY 3:
GOLDEN PASS PANORAMIC TRAIN – GLACIER 3000 – INTERLAKEN

A DAY OF ALPINE ADVENTURE, SCENIC TRAINS & MOUNTAIN THRILLS

GOLDEN PASS PANORAMIC TRAIN – SCENIC SWISS COUNTRYSIDE
After breakfast, we head to the picturesque village of Zweisimmen to board the Golden Pass Panoramic Train, renowned for its breathtaking views. Over the next 30 minutes, watch the Swiss countryside come alive outside your panoramic windows:

  • Lush green meadows dotted with grazing cows
  • Charming wooden chalets
  • Majestic peaks of the Alps forming a picture‑perfect backdrop

The train ride to Gstaad or Saanen is a visual feast and a perfect introduction to Switzerland’s natural beauty.

GLACIER 3000 – THRILLS ABOVE THE CLOUDS
Upon arrival in Gstaad or Saanen, our coach takes us on a short scenic drive to Col du Pillon, the gateway to Glacier 3000. We ascend in two panoramic cable cars, reaching an altitude of 3,000 metres in just 15 minutes.

SUMMIT HIGHLIGHTS

  • Peak Walk by Tissot – The world’s only suspension bridge connecting two mountain peaks
  • Spectacular panoramic views of the Matterhorn, Mont Blanc, and Jungfrau

ALPINE ACTIVITIES (WEATHER PERMITTING)

  • Ice Express chairlift
  • Snow Fun Park
  • Snowbus Glacier Tour
  • Alpine Coaster – the highest roller coaster in the world
  • Dog sled rides

Enjoy lunch at your leisure at one of the mountaintop restaurants, where the scenery rivals the cuisine.

ARRIVAL IN INTERLAKEN – LAKES & ALPINE CHARM
We then continue to Interlaken, a charming resort town nestled between Lake Brienz and Lake Thun, framed by towering alpine peaks. Take free time to explore and enjoy:

  • Kursaal Gardens – home to the statue of legendary Indian filmmaker Yash Chopra
  • Hoheweg Street – the town’s lively main street, lined with shops, cafes, and stunning mountain views

Interlaken offers a perfect blend of peaceful lakeside charm and vibrant alpine energy.

DINNER & OVERNIGHT STAY
After a day filled with scenic trains, mountain thrills, and tranquil lakes, we return to the hotel for a delicious dinner and a well‑earned overnight rest.

MEALS: B, D

DAY 4:
MT TITLIS – LUCERNE – BERN

A DAY OF ALPINE ADVENTURE, SWISS HERITAGE & CITY CHARM

ASCEND TO MT. TITLIS – A SPECTACULAR ALPINE EXPERIENCE
After breakfast, we check out from our hotel and head towards Engelberg to begin our unforgettable journey up Mt. Titlis. Our ascent starts with the Titlis Xpress gondola from Engelberg to Stand station. From here, we board the world’s first revolving cable car – Titlis Rotair, offering a breathtaking 360‑degree panorama as it transports us to the summit at 3,020 metres.

At the top, enjoy a range of exciting attractions:

  • Glacier Cave – Step into a magical world of ice and history.
  • Titlis Cliff Walk (subject to operation) – Europe’s highest suspension bridge at 3,041 metres.
  • Photo corner in traditional Swiss outfits.
  • Free time for snow activities, scenic relaxation, or coffee with stunning mountain views.

ARRIVAL IN LUCERNE – THE HEART OF SWITZERLAND
After descending to Engelberg, we continue to the iconic city of Lucerne, known for its blend of breathtaking natural beauty and rich cultural heritage. With its lakeside setting and mountain backdrop, Lucerne is a highlight of any Swiss journey.

CHAPEL BRIDGE & WATER TOWER
Discover the historic Chapel Bridge, Europe’s oldest covered wooden bridge, originally part of the city’s medieval fortifications. Admire the 17th‑century painted panels illustrating the history of Lucerne and Switzerland. Nearby stands the distinctive Water Tower, a striking landmark and symbol of the city. Take time to explore the charming old town, shop for Swiss souvenirs, or simply enjoy the tranquil views over Lake Lucerne and its postcard‑perfect surroundings.

LION MONUMENT – A MOVING TRIBUTE
We walk to the poignant Lion Monument, carved into natural rock to honour the Swiss Guards who lost their lives in 1792 during the French Revolution. Often called “the most mournful and moving piece of stone in the world,” this monument invites quiet reflection.

BERN – THE TIMELESS SWISS CAPITAL
We continue to Bern, the capital of Switzerland, known for its beautifully preserved medieval Old Town, which became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983. Enjoy a guided walking tour covering iconic landmarks such as:

  • Zytglogge (Clock Tower) – Built in 1191, this medieval tower is as old as the city itself.
  • Einstein House – The former residence of Albert Einstein, now a museum.
  • BärenPark (Bear Park) – Home to Bern’s beloved symbol, the bears.
  • And other charming corners of the Old Town.

DINNER & OVERNIGHT STAY
We conclude the day with a delicious Indian dinner before heading to our hotel for a comfortable overnight stay.

MEALS: B, D

DAY 5:
HOTEL – CALAIS/DUNKERQUE – LONDON

FAREWELL TO EUROPE & RETURN TO THE UK

MORNING DEPARTURE
After breakfast, check out from your hotel and settle into your comfortable coach as we begin our journey towards Calais or Dunkerque for the Channel crossing to Dover.

JOURNEY BACK TO LONDON
Upon arrival in Dover, continue your journey towards your destination. As the tour concludes, bid farewell to the friends and memories you’ve made during this unforgettable European adventure.

Please note: A vegetarian packed lunch will be provided today.

DAY 1:
LONDON – CALAIS – BRUSSELS – STRASBOURG

A JOURNEY THROUGH HISTORY, CULTURE & EUROPEAN CHARM

After a warm welcome from your tour manager at your designated pick-up point, settle into your comfortable coach as we begin our journey across the English Channel. Upon arrival in Calais or Dunkerque, we travel onwards into Belgium.

ARRIVAL IN BRUSSELS – WALKING TOUR OF THE OLD TOWN
Our first stop is the charming city of Brussels, where we begin with a guided walking tour of the historic old town. At the heart of the city lies the La Grand Place, one of the most beautiful and photographed squares in Europe. Surrounded by stunning guildhalls, the Town Hall, and the King’s House (also known as the Bread House), this UNESCO World Heritage Site is a true architectural masterpiece. The King’s House also houses the Museum of the City of Brussels, offering insights into the city’s rich heritage.

Nearby, you’ll encounter the bronze statue of Everard t’Serclaes, a local hero who died defending Brussels in the 15th century. Legend has it that touching his arm brings good luck.

MANNEKEN PIS – A BELOVED SYMBOL
A short walk leads us to Manneken Pis, a quirky and iconic statue that represents the spirit of Brussels. Created in 1388, this small 50 cm bronze figure of a boy urinating into a fountain has long been one of the city’s favourite symbols. It originally served as a public water source and is located just off the Grand Place, between Rue de l’Étuve and Rue du Chêne.

PHOTO STOP AT THE ATOMIUM
Next, we take a photo stop at the Atomium, the most iconic structure in Brussels. Standing 102 metres tall, this futuristic stainless-steel model of an atom was built for the 1958 Brussels World’s Fair and remains a powerful symbol of innovation. Today, the Atomium is to Brussels what the Eiffel Tower is to Paris.

JOURNEY TO STRASBOURG
In the evening, we depart Brussels and head towards Strasbourg. End your day with a delicious Indian dinner, which may be provided either at a local restaurant or at the hotel after check‑in, followed by a comfortable overnight stay.

MEALS: D

DAY 2:
BLACK FOREST – LAKE TITISEE – RHINE FALLS – LUCERNE

A DAY OF SCENIC BEAUTY, CULTURAL DISCOVERY & SWISS CHARM

JOURNEY INTO THE ENCHANTING BLACK FOREST
After breakfast, we board our comfortable coach and travel to Germany’s legendary Black Forest. With landscapes that look straight out of a Brothers Grimm fairy tale, this region offers a magical start to our day of exploration.

VISIT TO LAKE TITISEE
Our day begins with a visit to the famous Lake Titisee, located in the charming town of Titisee‑Neustadt. Formed during the last Ice Age, this crystal‑clear lake sits 850 m above sea level and stretches 2 km in length. One of the most popular destinations in the region, Titisee is ideal for swimming, sailing, windsurfing, pedal boating, and leisurely strolls along its picturesque promenade. Enjoy free time soaking in the Black Forest atmosphere, take a refreshing walk, or explore the local shops.

EXPERIENCE THE SPECTACULAR RHINE FALLS
Crossing into Switzerland, our first stop is Schaffhausen, home to the mighty Rhine Falls – Europe’s largest waterfall. Marvel at the thundering cascade of water spanning 150 metres in width. Adventurous travellers can take a thrilling boat ride and climb to the famous middle rock for an up‑close encounter with the roaring falls.

ARRIVAL IN LUCERNE – THE HEART OF SWITZERLAND
We continue to the iconic city of Lucerne, known for its blend of breathtaking natural beauty and rich cultural heritage. With its lakeside setting and mountain backdrop, Lucerne is a highlight of any Swiss journey.

CHAPEL BRIDGE & WATER TOWER
Discover the historic Chapel Bridge, Europe’s oldest covered wooden bridge, originally part of the city’s medieval fortifications. Admire the 17th‑century painted panels illustrating the history of Lucerne and Switzerland. Nearby stands the distinctive Water Tower, a striking landmark and symbol of the city. Take time to explore the charming old town, shop for Swiss souvenirs, or simply enjoy the tranquil views over Lake Lucerne and its postcard‑perfect surroundings.

LION MONUMENT – A MOVING TRIBUTE
We walk to the poignant Lion Monument, carved into natural rock to honour the Swiss Guards who lost their lives in 1792 during the French Revolution. Often called “the most mournful and moving piece of stone in the world,” this monument invites quiet reflection.

DINNER & OVERNIGHT STAY
End your day with a delicious Indian dinner, which may be provided either at a local restaurant or at the hotel after check‑in, followed by a comfortable overnight stay.

MEALS: B, L, D

DAY 3:
MT. TITLIS – INTERLAKEN – BERN

A DAY OF SNOW‑CAPPED PEAKS, ALPINE CHARM & SWISS HERITAGE

ASCEND TO MT. TITLIS – A SPECTACULAR ALPINE EXPERIENCE
After breakfast, we check out from our hotel and head towards Engelberg to begin our unforgettable journey up Mt. Titlis. Our ascent starts with the Titlis Xpress gondola from Engelberg to Stand station. From here, we board the world’s first revolving cable car – Titlis Rotair, offering a breathtaking 360‑degree panorama as it transports us to the summit at 3,020 metres.

At the top, enjoy a range of exciting attractions:

  • Glacier Cave – Step into a magical world of ice and history.
  • Titlis Cliff Walk (subject to operation) – Europe’s highest suspension bridge at 3,041 metres.
  • Photo corner in traditional Swiss outfits.
  • Free time for snow activities, scenic relaxation, or coffee with stunning mountain views.

INTERLAKEN – BETWEEN TWO SPARKLING LAKES
After lunch, we travel to Interlaken, a charming resort town set in a narrow valley between Lake Brienz and Lake Thun. Nestled in the Bernese Oberland, Interlaken is famous for its mountain scenery, peaceful lakes, and vibrant tourist culture.

Enjoy a stroll through:

  • Kursaal Garden, featuring a statue of the legendary Indian filmmaker Yash Chopra.
  • Hoheweg, Interlaken’s main street – perfect for shopping, relaxing, or admiring the Jungfrau views.

BERN – THE TIMELESS SWISS CAPITAL
We continue to Bern, the capital of Switzerland, known for its beautifully preserved medieval Old Town, which became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.

Enjoy a guided walking tour covering iconic landmarks such as:

  • Zytglogge (Clock Tower) – Built in 1191, this medieval tower is as old as the city itself.
  • Einstein House – The former residence of Albert Einstein, now a museum.
  • BärenPark (Bear Park) – Home to Bern’s beloved symbol, the bears.
  • And other charming corners of the Old Town.

DINNER & OVERNIGHT STAY
We conclude our day with a delicious Indian dinner, which may be provided either at a local restaurant or at the hotel after check‑in, followed by a comfortable overnight stay.

MEALS: B, L, D

DAY 4:
PARIS

AN ICONIC ARRIVAL IN FRANCE’S GLITTERING CAPITAL

SCENIC JOURNEY TO PARIS
After enjoying breakfast, check out from the hotel and settle into your comfortable coach as we begin our journey towards the enchanting French capital – Paris. We make a brief stop en route for packed lunch before arriving in the city by late afternoon.

EIFFEL TOWER – PARIS FROM THE SKY
Upon arrival, we head straight to one of the world’s most iconic landmarks – the Eiffel Tower.

Ascend to the top floor and take in breathtaking panoramic views of Paris. Experience a spectacular journey to the summit, where stunning vistas of the city await. Named after engineer Gustave Eiffel, whose company designed and built it between 1887 and 1889, the tower stands at 330 metres (1,083 ft) – roughly the height of an 81‑storey building – and remains the tallest structure in Paris. Prepare to be swept away by awe and excitement as you ascend this architectural marvel.

INDIAN DINNER & PARIS BY NIGHT TOUR
In the evening, enjoy a delicious Indian dinner before embarking on a “Paris by Night” tour. See the city sparkle as you pass glittering landmarks such as the grand Champs‑Élysées and the majestic Arc de Triomphe to the dazzling Eiffel Tower, all beautifully illuminated.

Experience the romance and magic of Paris under the night sky – an unforgettable way to end your day. After the enchanting tour, return to your hotel for a comfortable overnight stay, ready for more adventures tomorrow.

Please note: Today vegetarian packed lunch will be provided.

MEALS: B, L, D

DAY 5:
PARIS – LONDON

A SCENIC FAREWELL TO FRANCE & JOURNEY BACK TO THE UK

MORNING IN PARIS & SEINE RIVER CRUISE
After breakfast, we check out of the hotel and make our way to the city centre of Paris. Experience Paris from a fresh and captivating angle with a panoramic boat cruise on the River Seine aboard elegant, glass‑topped vessels. As you glide along the river, admire iconic landmarks that define the heritage of Paris, such as the Eiffel Tower, Louvre Museum, Notre‑Dame Cathedral, Musée d’Orsay and more. This relaxing cruise offers a unique perspective, revealing the historic heart of Paris from the gentle flow of the Seine.

CHANNEL CROSSING TO THE UK
After lunch, we begin our journey towards Calais or Dunkerque for our Channel crossing to Dover. Enjoy the scenic transition as we leave the European mainland and return to the United Kingdom.

FAREWELL & END OF TOUR
Upon arrival in Dover, we proceed towards our destination. Your memorable tour concludes here, as we bid farewell to the wonderful friends and experiences shared along the journey.

MEALS: B, L

We will try to make sufficient comfort stops. On rare occasions, your coach may not have a WC or TV/DVD facility on board. All coaches are either air-conditioned or air-cooled. We have a strict “no smoking” policy on all our coaches. Consumption of alcohol is prohibited on all our coaches. During transfers, we may use an alternative vehicle (smaller coaches) which may not have the above facilities.

BAGGAGE ON COACH
Each passenger occupying a seat is allowed to carry one piece of luggage whose maximum weight should not be more than 20kg and not exceeding dimensions of 90 x 75 x 43cm / 35 x 29 x 16 inches and one piece of hand luggage whose weight should not be more than 8kg and not exceeding dimensions of 20 x 20 x 48 cm / 8 x 8 x 19 inches which can fit under their seat or in the overhead compartment. The main luggage will be placed inside the coach locker and the passenger will only get access to the same when we reach the hotel in the night.

The driver will load and unload one piece of luggage per person from the coach. Since there is no porter service provided, passengers will be required to carry their own luggage from the coach to the hotel rooms and therefore one piece of main luggage and one small hand luggage is recommended. We also recommend that children or family members not sharing a room have separate luggage as rooms cannot be guaranteed adjoining or nearby.

It is advisable to put your name and address on each piece of luggage as many passengers have similar bags and this avoids confusion. If for any reasons your baggage or personal valuable is lost or stolen, you must report it to the tour manager, or in the absence of a tour manager to the local police or hotel. Gowri Tours cannot accept any responsibility for your personal belongings.

If your baggage is over and above the limits mentioned here or if you arrive with extra luggage, an additional fee of £10 per bag per day will apply (subject to availability). All baggage is placed at the owner’s risk, and Gowri Tours or its suppliers accept no liability for loss or damage to bags caused anyhow.

CHILDREN & YOUNG INFANTS
Children and young infants are welcome to travel on our tours. Children under the age of 23 months will be charged an infant fare on all tours. Car/booster seats are not provided on coaches by Gowri Tours, and it is strongly recommended carrying your own which can fit within the coach seats. Coaches will not provide any cold or hot water to heat up or cool milk bottles. It is passengers’ responsibility to make sure of necessary arrangements for any children in their group.

Restaurants or hotels will not provide any milk or baby food and passengers are advised to carry prepared baby milk cartons/powder and baby foods whilst on tour. Please also note that not all hotels provide a kettle, so if hot water is required for warming milk etc. in the hotel, then it is advisable to carry a bottle warmer / kettle (do not forget your adapter). Pushchairs should be foldable and will be kept in the luggage compartment of the coach. Children’s or infants will not be seated at the front of the coach.

TOUR MANAGER
Professional tour manager/driver or local guides throughout your itinerary accompany all our escorted tours. On rare occasions, your tour manager may not meet you at your dedicated pick-up point but at a later stage; the driver will be there to take care of your needs. On rare occasions, a tour manager will not be available to accompany you; this would be due to unavoidable operational issues, or we will be utilising local guides for their wealth of experience. On rare occasion on some of our tours, there will be no accompanying tour manager and our expert driver or local tour guide will conduct the tour.

WEATHER, CLOTHING & ACCESSORIES
It is recommended to always carry an umbrella and a jacket. We recommend that you visit www.weather.com to ensure you have an idea of the weather at the time of the year you want to travel and can be well prepared by ensuring that you are carrying appropriate clothing, footwear, and accessories. Passengers should also be aware that some sightseeing would be done after dusk.

During summer months, it is advisable to wear light garments during the day but keep a light jacket or sweater in your hand luggage for the evening, as it can get quite chilly. Also, few other items which are highly recommended are a family sized umbrella, rain wear, pair of sunglasses, pair of trainers or comfortable walking shoes especially for certain excursions that involve a considerable amount of walking. We also recommend passengers to carry a small travel iron, hairdryer, kettle etc. as not all hotels may provide the same in the rooms. You may also be required to be “covered” up when visiting certain places; if you are unsure what to take then please do discuss with us and we will be happy to assist.

HOTELS
The hotels on our tours are selected carefully to ensure that a minimum 3* category is provided (overseas ratings are classified by each country’s own tourist board) and can be located either close to the city you are visiting or on the outskirts. Facilities vary from hotel to hotel and include en‑suite bath or shower and generally a TV and telephone. Some of the rooms may have mini bars and 24‑hour room service. You will be charged to use any payable facilities at the hotel to your room and payable on check out.

Most hotels may require a credit card to cover your extras or cash deposits. Please remember that most hotels in Europe have small rooms unlike many other countries and not all hotels will have air‑conditioning or lift as standard. If you have difficulty with stairs, please advise us so we can try to request a room on a low floor. Rooms are allocated by the hotel so some guests may get larger or different type of rooms to other guests. We do not have control over this. Some hotels may provide 2 single beds joined together as a double bed.

Note: Gowri Tours reserves the right to substitute hotels whilst passengers are on tour to a similar standard due to unforeseen circumstances. Please note that hotel’s normal check‑in times are from late afternoon, e.g. 3pm, and checkout around 11am, but it does vary from hotel to hotel.

ROOM CONFIGURATION
Most hotels can only accommodate a maximum of three persons in each room. If you are a family of four, i.e., two adults and two children, and prefer all to be in one room, then your first child will be given an extra bed, but the second child will be required to share the double bed as no extra bed can be provided. The extra bed provided will be either a sofa bed or rollaway bed. These extra beds may not be full sized as double beds and are usually suitable for one individual only.

The cost of the package is based on a minimum of two adults sharing one room. If your group consists of one adult and one child, the child must pay a full adult fare to make up the cost for the room required. Baby cots are not guaranteed. When you opt for two rooms, each room must have an adult accompanying a child as per regulations of the hotel. A child will always have to be accompanied by an adult in a room. We will try our best to get these 2 rooms next to each other but can’t guarantee the same. Where a quad room is not available for your group, a reduction will be given as stated in the itinerary. Note that quad rooms have limited space and additional beds may not be suitable for tall adults. Any damages within the room or hotel you are staying in will be payable at the time of checkout by the passenger.

MEALS
Breakfast is normally continental buffet, which will be served in the hotel that you will be staying. All other pre‑booked meals will be either in the hotel’s own restaurant or at an outside restaurant and are not changeable. Passengers may have an option to choose from vegetarian or non‑vegetarian (wherever possible Jain/Halal) meals. The meals will only include the food; all extras i.e., alcohol, beverages or any extra items requested by you will need to be settled by you directly with the restaurant. Any meals not taken will not be reimbursed under any circumstances.

Lunches are vegetarian only and will be served outdoors at a service station/rest area where limited or no seating is available. Lunch is served in a picnic‑style buffet arrangement. On some days, you may be provided with packed lunches or dinners to suit the itinerary of a particular tour. We endeavour to book Indian meals wherever possible, however due to local constraints if we are unable to do so, we will offer local vegetarian options. If you have any specific dietary needs or allergies, you must inform us at the time of booking, so we can inform the caterer. However, special arrangements for food cannot be guaranteed for allergies or requests such as Halal or Jain meals. Passengers with severe food allergies are advised to make appropriate arrangements prior to commencing their tour. Gowri Tours reserves the right to change meal arrangement in circumstances that are beyond our control.

If for any reason we are unable to provide the meal, we will refund the passenger with 10 GBP/EURO for lunch and 12 GBP/EURO per dinner.

SEATING, DIETARY OR ROOM ALLOCATION AND OTHER REQUESTS
Gowri Tours works at times with intermediary agents (airlines, hotels, transport companies, other suppliers etc.) to arrange your holiday. If passengers have special requirements such as a rooming request, or a special meal request etc., then they should advise Gowri Tours at the time of booking. Any special requests cannot be guaranteed by Gowri Tours. Seating requests are not taken under any circumstance. Seating is allocated by booking reference number however, there are some exceptions to this, i.e., group sizes, coach size, promotional seating, H&S laws, pickups, company discretion etc.

We do not promise or guarantee any specific seat on the coach, and we have the sole right to assign your seats. Any indication is for reference only and is subject to change regardless of whether given in writing or any other means. Seat numbers will be allocated to all passengers on the day of departure. Groups with children will not be seated in the front of the coach even if they have booked very early. Some seats in the coach may not recline. Passengers who do not wish to book together but wish to travel together must inform Gowri Tours at the time of booking so they can be seated next to each other. Any medical and/or personal grounds are not considered when allocating seats, unless explicitly stated by law or governing bodies.

CREDIT CARD & CURRENCIES
We recommend that you take a credit or debit card on holiday with you, as it provides extra financial flexibility. Many restaurants, shops and hotels accept major international credit cards, such as Visa or MasterCard. It is also possible to draw cash with your credit or debit card at some banks and cash machines, though this will incur a fee charged by your card provider.

Note: Advise your bank which countries you are visiting prior to travel so that you do not run the risk of your card being refused and subsequent expensive phone calls to unlock it. Currency of the EU countries is Euros. Some countries use their own currency along with Euros, e.g. in Switzerland the currency is Swiss Francs. We recommend all our passengers to convert any spending money they need before their travel, as we will not be able to take you to a money exchange place. If you need more local currency when abroad, we recommend that you exchange money at a bank rather than at hotels, as they will charge high commission rates. You may also need your passport for identification as you would for travellers’ cheques. Even though in Europe credit and debit cards are widely accepted, keep in mind the exchange rate may be poor and commission will be charged. Always carry some EURO coins whilst on tour as you may need to pay for toilets in many parts of Europe.

PASSPORTS & VISAS
All passengers require a passport for travel outside the UK. It is the responsibility of the passenger to have a passport that is valid for 6 months from the date of completing the tour. Gowri Tours will attempt to supply passengers with the most up to date information regarding the visa requirements for the destinations that they will travel. However, as visa stipulations change frequently, we advise passengers to inquire with the relevant consulate as to the exact requirements, which they must fulfil in good time prior to their travel date. Gowri Tours cannot take responsibility for cancellation due to lack of correct visa requirements, as it is the passenger’s responsibility to ensure that these requirements are fulfilled prior to their tour departure. For further information on visas please contact Gowri Tours or visit www.mantraholidays.co.uk.

LOST PROPERTY & THEFT
It is passenger’s responsibility to ensure that your property and valuables are always safe. If an item has been left in a hotel, restaurant, coach etc. you will need to call the respective supplier and arrange with them directly for the return of your item. Gowri Tours will not carry anyone’s left property across international borders whether it is authorised in writing or by any other means. In case of theft, you will need to advise your tour manager immediately and report the theft to the nearest police personnel who will provide you with a police report or crime reference number. You are advised not to carry unnecessary valuables and to be always vigilant, as tourist spots are well known targets for pickpockets. Gowri Tours recommends all passengers to have valid travel insurance, including EU citizens.

PHONE CARDS & VOLTAGE
All phone calls made from your hotel room phone are chargeable. This charge can be high, especially for international calls. It is always cheaper to use public telephones. If using your mobile phone during tour, we suggest that you check with your service provider if it will incur any charges.

Electrical currents vary between Britain, the European continent, and North America. We suggest you carry a converter for your electric shaver, travelling iron, hair dryer, and other small appliances. We recommend that you purchase a universal travel adapter before travel to charge all your gadgets.

LONG DISTANCE JOURNEYS
As the distance in Europe is vast, some journeys will be long, and they are unavoidable when travelling from one city to another. Hence, Gowri Tours recommends on such long journey days to wear comfortable clothes. As most part of these days will be spent inside the coach, we advise passengers to carry all necessities that they may need for the day such as water, dry snacks, tissues, medication, power bank, chargers etc. with them in their hand luggage.

EXCURSIONS
Due to many visitors, there may be waiting times and queuing times involved, which can be anything up to 4 hours. These times may be modified without notice by the management due to exceptional events, unfavourable weather conditions, large numbers of visitors, or a Force Majeure event. Access to the excursions/monuments depends on the type of ticket purchased, and all exits are final; no re‑entries are permitted. No refunds will be made if access is restricted due to poor weather conditions or a decision by the public authorities. Tickets issued are for immediate entry. In the case of loss or theft, the tickets cannot be reimbursed. Certain excursions may restrict access due to saturation.

ITINERARY & TIME KEEPING
The tour manager reserves the right to modify the itinerary during the tour. These changes may occur due to unexpected delays, major local events that can often arise or a Force Majeure event. Time keeping is the most important aspect of a group tour and all passengers must adhere to the timings given by their tour manager. All our holiday packages are subject to governance by DVSA for driving hours hence it is the passenger’s responsibility to ensure all departure times are respected. Gowri Tours will not take responsibility for passengers left behind due to not adhering to itineraries and times stated by the tour manager for whatsoever reason, and any subsequent impact this may cause financially or non‑financially. It is a passenger’s responsibility to ensure that they are clear in understanding of the departure time from any given point. If in any doubt, please make sure that you recheck the departure timings again with your tour manager and follow the same.

We request you to go through the general information and Terms & Conditions before booking and travelling.
